question: What is the main function of the crypts of Lieberkühn in the colon?
explanation: The crypts in the large intestine secrete mucus that helps lubricate stool and protects the colon wall. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h1)

question: If a patient has their entire colon surgically removed, which major problem is expected?

options.A: Total inability to break down sugars
options.B: Severe trouble reabsorbing water and body salts

explanation: The main job of the large intestine is to recover water and salts from waste before it leaves the body. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h1)

question: Which test allows a doctor to look directly at the entire lining of the colon?
explanation: A colonoscopy lets the doctor view the whole large intestine, from the rectum all the way up to the cecum. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h2)

question: Why can a flexible sigmoidoscopy not show problems in the upper part of the colon?

options.A: It cannot be used to take tissue samples
options.B: It exposes the patient to high radiation
options.C: It only looks at the rectum and sigmoid colon
options.D: It requires general surgery and anesthesia

explanation: A sigmoidoscopy only covers the lower third of the large intestine, so it misses issues higher up in the colon. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h2)

question: Which feature helps tell Crohn's disease apart from ulcerative colitis?

options.B: Inflammation limited strictly to the rectum
options.C: Continuous inflammation starting from the rectum
options.D: Patches of healthy tissue mixed with diseased areas anywhere in the GI tract

explanation: Crohn's disease features patchy, inflamed areas mixed with healthy tissue, often called skip lesions. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h3)

question: A patient with ulcerative colitis suddenly has a swollen, hard belly, fever, and fast heart rate. What serious complication is likely happening?
explanation: Toxic megacolon is a dangerous, rapid swelling of the colon seen in severe cases, with a high risk of bursting. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h3)

question: What common diet issue is linked to developing diverticulosis?
explanation: Low-fiber diets lead to hard stools that require heavy straining, which pushes out weak spots in the colon wall. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h4)

question: Which part of the abdomen is usually most painful during an attack of acute diverticulitis?
explanation: Because small pouches (diverticula) most often form in the lower left part of the colon, pain usually shows up there. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h4)

question: What is the main difference between Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) and Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD)?

options.A: IBS causes high levels of C-reactive protein
options.B: IBS causes deep ulcers in the colon wall
options.C: IBS has no visible tissue damage or structural changes
options.D: IBS permanently destroys the colon lining

explanation: IBS is a functional disorder, meaning the bowel looks completely normal during tests even though it does not work smoothly. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h5)

question: A patient with IBS-D has frequent watery stools every morning. Which diet change is best to suggest?

options.A: Eating more raw garlic and onions

explanation: Low-FODMAP diets cut down on specific carbs that pull extra water into the bowel, helping to manage diarrhea. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h5)

question: Which type of colonic polyp has the highest chance of turning into cancer?
explanation: Adenomatous polyps are considered pre-cancerous and can turn into cancer over time if left alone. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h6)

question: Why are routine screening colonoscopies so helpful in stopping colorectal cancer?

options.A: They completely cure advanced cancer tumors
options.B: They remove the patient's genetic risk for cancer
options.C: They allow doctors to remove pre-cancerous polyps before cancer starts

explanation: Finding and cutting out adenomatous polyps during a colonoscopy stops them from turning into cancer later. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h6)

question: What is the most common physical cause of a large bowel blockage in adults?
explanation: Tumors growing inside the hollow space of the colon cause most large bowel blockages. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h7)

question: Why is a blocked bowel with trapped gas and fluid on both ends treated as a surgical emergency?

options.A: It immediately stops breathing by pressing on the diaphragm
options.B: High pressure inside quickly cuts off blood supply and can cause the bowel to burst
options.C: It causes instant high blood pressure and stroke
options.D: It stops the kidneys from cleaning the blood

explanation: When a section of the bowel is sealed off, trapped pressure cuts off blood flow, leading to tissue death and tears. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h7)

question: What should a healthy, normal intestinal stoma look like right after surgery?
explanation: A healthy stoma should look pink or red and stay moist, which shows it has good blood flow. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h8)

question: Which assessment finding in a patient with acute diverticulitis means you should call the doctor immediately?

options.A: Passing small hard stools every two days
options.C: Mild pain in the lower left belly when pressed
options.D: A rigid, board-like belly that hurts when you let go

explanation: A rigid, board-like abdomen is a sign of severe irritation in the abdominal cavity, often meaning the bowel has burst. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h8)
